subject: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Rossi <luca.rossi@finbank.eu>, FinBank IT <it@finbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Luca — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align with compliance and infra teams.

Summary of requirements I captured:
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer PII and logs; APAC support for Southeast region later in the year.
- Evaluation criteria: strict data-at-rest residency (no cross-border backups), auditability (audit logs + SOC2 evidence), and predictable latency for customer-facing workflows (95th pct. target ~200ms for lookup flows).
- Deployment modes under consideration: Hosted API (eu region), Dedicated reserved capacity (single-tenant GPU pool in eu-west), Private VPC / on-prem for strict residency.

Notes / clarifications from call:
- You indicated procurement prefers a solution that avoids exporting customer data outside the EU for backups and long-term storage.
- You want options and rough timelines for Dedicated vs Private so you can slot into procurement and network change windows.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary of controls) and deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (side-by-side Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether your legal team requires zero-cross-border replication (i.e., backups and failover excluded from leaving the EU)?
2) Expected peak concurrent RPS / tokens per minute for the pilot (helps sizing Dedicated).
3) Who should I loop in from procurement/network security (name + email) so we can share a detailed network requirements doc and timeline?

I'll set up a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) to walk the FinBank infra team through network requirements and deployment diagrams. Proposed slots: Tue 2027-03-30 09:00-10:00 CET or Wed 2027-03-31 14:00-15:00 CET — let me know what works.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Aditya Rao

Hi Aditya — thanks for the summary and the docs. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) On Hosted API (EU region) — does data-at-rest and backups stay exclusively in the EU by default? We need to know if any backups or warm replicas can end up in the US for disaster recovery.
2) For Private / on-prem: what's the typical lead time and what are the minimal network requirements? Our infra calendar is tight for Q2.
3) For Dedicated: can you provide a rough pricing band for a pilot (capacity to handle ~200 RPS peak, burst to 400 for 10-minute windows)? Procurement wants a ballpark for planning.

Procurement is expecting to review options by mid-April. Please also include any standard SOC2 evidence and any attestations on EU-only storage.

Best,

Hi Luca — great questions, answers below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Hosted API (EU region)
- By default, requests routed to our eu-west region are processed and stored in datastores located in EU-based zones. Short-term caches and KV caches are regional.
- Backups and cross-region replication are configurable. For most Hosted customers we maintain cross-region backups for DR, but we can configure EU-only backups and disable cross-region replicas at the account level with contractual attestation (this is a common request for EU-regulated customers).
- Caveat: some global telemetry (anonymized usage metrics) is aggregated outside the EU unless you select an enterprise data partitioning option. We can provide an attestation and SOC2 artifacts next week.

2) Dedicated reserved capacity
- Pricing band for pilot sized ~200 RPS (burst to 400): roughly €15k–€30k/month depending on model family and quantization profile. Exact pricing requires expected token/seq distribution.
- Lead time: typically 4–6 weeks for pool provisioning and network peering in eu-west.

3) Private VPC / on-prem
- Typical timeline: 8–12 weeks (depends on procurement, network CAB windows, and whether on-prem hardware is provided by the customer).
- Minimal network requirements (high level):
  - Inbound TLS endpoints (port 443) for control-plane callbacks
  - Outbound NAT to our patch/update endpoints (we provide IP ranges)
  - 10 Gbps peering recommended for production-grade RPS at the scale you mentioned
  - VPN or Direct Connect / Interconnect options supported

Attachments and next actions:
- I've uploaded a Mutual Action Plan template and a more detailed network requirements doc to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFinBank-MAP (link shared).
- SOC2 artifacts: we'll share the SOC2 package with procurement under an NDA — I'm happy to coordinate with your legal team.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (Marissa + solutions) to walk your infra/security team through the network diagram and account-level controls — proposed slot Tue 2027-03-30 09:00 CET (45 mins). If that works I will send calendar invite.
2) I will scope a Dedicated pilot estimate and send a written band by EOD Wed 2027-03-31.
3) If you want strict EU-only guarantees (no cross-border backups or telemetry), the recommended path is Dedicated with EU-only backups or Private VPC with contractual data residency language; we can start contract/legal conversations once you confirm preference.

Let me know your availability for the tech call and who from procurement/netsec to include.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

— Aditya Rao
